DE-7_DE-15_release_lock_noop.red_observed: 2 failed — DE-7 and DE-15 both red
DE-7_DE-15_release_lock_noop.probe_engine_inspection: GENUINE. _probe_lock_is_free calls create_async_engine(dsn, pool_size=1, max_overflow=0) — a NEW engine with its own pool, therefore a distinct PG backend session. PG advisory locks are re-entrant within one backend, so a same-pool checkout could draw the lock-holding connection and report 'free'; the separate engine removes that. Verified by code inspection AND empirically (fixed gate goes red where execute-agent's first same-pool version stayed green).

row_index_dropped_and_lock_stubbed.expected: the plan's stated DE-9b falsifier — duplicate EXPIRE rows appear

row_index_dropped_and_lock_stubbed.finding: Removing uq_coop_ledger_expire_per_lot does not permit duplicate rows — it breaks the ON CONFLICT inference outright (see F-B), so every insert fails. DE-9b's `dupes == 0` assertion therefore has NO known falsifier and is effectively unfalsified. Only its `total == _N_LOTS` companion assertion carries signal.

F_B_independent_verification.claim: with uq_coop_ledger_expire_per_lot removed, the sweep writes 0 rows and emits coop_expire_lot_failed
F_B_independent_verification.method: migration mutated to omit create_index; fresh disposable container; ran DE-7 (5 seeded lapsed lots) with --log-cli-level=INFO
F_B_independent_verification.observed: structlog error event `coop_expire_lot_failed lot_id=5078734a-...` plus asyncpg InvalidColumnReferenceError: 'there is no unique or exclusion constraint matching the ON CONFLICT specification'
F_B_independent_verification.mechanism: _EXPIRE_INSERT_SQL's ON CONFLICT clause infers its arbiter from the partial unique index. With the index absent PG cannot resolve the arbiter and raises per lot; the per-lot except swallows it as coop_expire_lot_failed and continues, so the sweep completes 'successfully' having expired NOTHING.
F_B_independent_verification.production_significance: Real robustness hole. If the index is ever absent (migration not applied, manual drop, restore from a pre-b7e4d21a9c58 dump) co-op credit expiry silently stops entirely on a billing surface, with only an error-level log line as signal. Fails silent, not loud.

G-20_residual_i_lock_acquisition_ungated.closed_by: DE-6 — acquisition observed from a third connection AND via the loser's `coop_expiry_sweep_skipped_locked` branch, never by row count.

G-20_residual_ii_release_proven_in_test_.reason: DE-7 is GREEN, but green here only shows the unlock landed on the lock-holding connection in a lane that runs ONE sweep with no competing pool consumer, so the session reliably re-draws its own connection after each per-lot commit. The documented residual — that under real contention another consumer takes that connection between commits, so the unlock runs elsewhere and silently no-ops — is NOT exercised. The lane bounds the residual (not reproducible without concurrent pool pressure) but does not eliminate it. coop_expiry_sweep.py's own docstring still records it as accepted.

G-20_residual_iii_aborted_transaction_pa.closed_by: DE-15 — an aborted session (SELECT 1/0) followed by a raise still leaves the lock free, observed from a SEPARATE-POOL probe engine.
G-20_residual_iii_aborted_transaction_pa.tester_confirmation: Mutation-probed: _release_lock no-op turns DE-15 RED. The separate-pool probe was inspected and is a genuinely distinct PG backend, so the re-entrancy vacuity that defeated the first version is closed.

findings.title: DE-5 is an intermittent gate (~10% red)
findings.detail: test_de5_scheduler_writes_expire_row failed 2 of ~20 full-file runs, unloaded as well as loaded. Passes 6/6 when run alone. Execute-agent reported a clean 7/7. A latency probe measuring the EXPIRE row immediately after _run_job_now() returns found the row already present in 15/15 attempts, so the obvious submission-vs-completion race is NOT confirmed as the mechanism. Root cause unresolved.
findings.impact: A flaky gate in a lane whose entire purpose is trustworthy evidence. Any future EVL run has a ~10% chance of a spurious red on this gate.

findings.title: DE-9b's duplicate-detection leg has no working falsifier
findings.detail: The plan's stated DE-9b falsifier (drop uq_coop_ledger_expire_per_lot while the lock is stubbed) does not produce duplicate rows. Removing the index breaks ON CONFLICT arbiter inference outright, so every insert errors (see F-B) and the children hang until timeout. The `dupes == 0` assertion is therefore unfalsified by any known mutation; only `total == _N_LOTS` carries signal.
findings.impact: Plan section E-3's reasoning is partly wrong. Documentation/contract defect, not a source defect.
